why:
LANDED 2026-09-03 (phase-379 W6, decision 3). The C API shipped this query TWICE, tier-disjoint, and BOTH spellings collapsed "did the query work" into "what is the answer". They are now ONE function in rcl's shape:

    rcl_ret_t rclc_action_server_get_active_goal_count(struct rcl_action_server_t *server, size_t *out);

Return code = did the call work; out-param = the answer. Upstream ships no count function at all, so there is no name to match; the SHAPE is matched instead, from the nearest neighbour `rcl_action_server_get_goal_handles(server, ***goal_handles, size_t *num_goals) -> rcl_ret_t`, which reports its count exactly this way. The name did not move -- `get_` STAYS. That was settled in W5 and re-affirmed here: 49 `nros_*_get_*` functions ship, our only other two count queries (`rclc_executor_get_handle_count`, `nros_parameter_server_get_count`) both use it, and W5 group A deliberately ADDED `get_` to C when `nros_lifecycle_get_state` became `..._get_current_state`.

WHAT THE MERGE HAD TO PRESERVE. The two halves were never one field behind two names; they read different storage, selected by `rcl_action_server_t::state`, and the merged function branches on that state rather than unifying the paths:
* `RCLC_ACTION_SERVER_STATE_INITIALIZED` (L2 callback tier) -> the executor arena, via `ActionServerRawHandle::active_goal_count(executor)` -> `as_raw_active_goal_count` -> `entry.core.active_goal_count()`.
* `NROS_ACTION_SERVER_STATE_POLLING` (L1 polling tier) -> the `ActionServerCore` living inline in `_opaque`, no executor and no arena indirection, behind `#[cfg(feature = "rmw-cffi")]`.

ERROR MAPPING, which is the half the old pair got wrong in two different ways. `RCL_RET_INVALID_ARGUMENT`: `server` or `out` is NULL. `RCL_RET_NOT_INIT`: the server is UNINITIALIZED or SHUTDOWN (neither tier claims it); or INITIALIZED but never registered with an executor, or already finalised; or POLLING in a build without `rmw-cffi`, where `nros_action_server_init_polling` sets the state outside the feature gate and leaves `_opaque` empty. `RCL_RET_OK`: `*out` holds the count, which may legitimately be 0. `*out` is left UNTOUCHED on every error path, so an ignored return code reads back the caller's own initialiser instead of a fabricated zero -- the ambiguity the old `size_t` spelling could not escape, since it answered 0 for NULL, for the wrong state, and for a genuinely empty goal set alike. The old `int32_t` half's tri-state is carried FORWARD, not deleted: it distinguished INVALID_ARGUMENT from NOT_INIT, and so does this.

THE OLD CALLBACK-TIER SPELLING GETS NO FORWARDER, and cannot. It was `size_t rclc_action_server_get_active_goal_count(const struct rcl_action_server_t *)` -- the same identifier the merged function now uses -- and C has one declaration per identifier, so there is no way to keep it alive beside the replacement. Its callers get a hard compile error (too few arguments, or a `size_t` initialised from an `rcl_ret_t`), which is the right failure for a signature change: the alternative would be a silent semantic swap where `0` stops meaning "error" and starts meaning "success". This was only affordable because the pair had ZERO callers anywhere in the tree, re-verified at merge time. The polling-tier spelling DOES get a forwarder; see `c:action_server_active_goal_count_raw`.

WHY THE W5 RECOMMENDATION WAS OVERRULED. The row previously recommended (a) -- keep both, re-verdict the pair `extension` -- on the grounds that a merge deletes an error channel. W6 found the premise backwards: the merge does not have to pick one of the two bad channels, because rcl's two-channel shape carries strictly more than either. `size_t` return loses the error; `int32_t` return loses the callback tier's type AND caps the count; `rcl_ret_t` + `size_t *out` loses nothing. What remains true from W5 is that BOTH functions were ours-only in both directions -- rcl/rclc has no active-goal count and C++ has only `ActionServer::for_each_active_goal`, which already returns `Result` and hands the answer to a visitor, i.e. does not collapse and needs no change.

GATED. `packages/api/nros-c/tests/compile/action_goal_count_entry_point.c` pins the merged signature by taking a function POINTER, which is also what proves the old `size_t` form is gone, on the `just check c` lane beside the W5 parameter and service entry points. It used to pin the deprecated forwarder's `int32_t` convention as well, and `action_deprecation_probe.c` asserted that forwarder still WARNED under `-Werror=deprecated-declarations`; phase-417 W-B5 (stage 6 step B, commit 4dc5caee9, 2026-09-05) retired the forwarder, deleted that probe (an expected-failure compile whose identifier is gone passes while asserting nothing) and trimmed the entry-point TU to its live half.

ORIGINAL ROW (W5, 2026-08-27), kept because it is the record of how the pair was diagnosed: OUR LANGUAGES DISAGREE, and inside one language: the C API ships this query TWICE. `rclc_action_server_get_active_goal_count` returns `size_t` for the callback tier and `nros_action_server_active_goal_count_raw` returns `int32_t` for the polling tier. One says `get_`, the other does not. Rust spells it `active_goal_count` on all four of its action types (RFC-430, a RUST convention that does not reach C, which is why Rust is also correct); C++ has no count at all. `_raw` is a systematic polling-tier suffix on 24 functions, so it constrained no callback-tier name. Same shape as the service stage's `c:client_server_available` / `c:client_service_is_ready`.
